title: Coherent finite residue systems and completed realization of an integral representation
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian separated scheme on which the prime $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix a geometric point $\bar x$ and the profinite group $\Pi=\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite, with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite free $A$-module of rank $r\geq0$, with a $\Pi$-action by $A$-linear automorphisms, jointly continuous for the $\varpi$-adic topology. Set $A_n=A/\varpi^n$ and $\Lambda_n=\Lambda/\varpi^n\Lambda$ for $n\geq1$.

There are finite locally constant etale $A_n$-module sheaves $F_n$, etale locally free of rank $r$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and equivariant fibre identifications $(F_n)_{\bar x}\cong\Lambda_n$ under the finite-coefficient Galois correspondence [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1). The actions on the finite sets $\Lambda_n$ are continuous for the discrete topology. There are transition maps $t_{n,j}:F_n\to F_j$ for all $n\geq j\geq1$, linear for $A_n\to A_j$, whose fibre maps are the quotient maps $\Lambda_n\to\Lambda_j$. They satisfy $t_{n,n}=1$ and $t_{j,i}t_{n,j}=t_{n,i}$. Their adjoints
$$A_j\otimes_{A_n}F_n\xrightarrow{\sim}F_j$$
are isomorphisms, compatible with the tensor associativity maps for every $n\geq j\geq i$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and let $\nu_X^*$ be the etale-to-pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Then $N_\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n$, with the induced $B_X$-action, is locally free of rank $r$, and the limit projections induce compatible isomorphisms $N_\Lambda/\varpi^nN_\Lambda\cong\nu_X^*F_n$. The construction, including the transitions, adjoint isomorphisms and limit projections, is functorial in continuous equivariant $A$-linear maps of finite free modules.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), pp. 59-60, and the integral-lattice construction in the proof of Lemma 7.4.7, p. 70; finite Galois correspondence and coherent residue transitions as in literature/stanford-weil2-seminar/L19.pdf, Proposition 1.1.9, third bullet

proof.text: Choose an $A$-basis of $\Lambda$, identifying $\Lambda_n$ with $A_n^r$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a DVR with finite residue field $k=A/(\varpi)$. Multiplication by $\varpi^a$ identifies $k$ with $\varpi^aA/\varpi^{a+1}A$: injectivity follows by cancellation in the domain $A$. The filtration by these subquotients shows that $A_n$ and $\Lambda_n$ are finite. The action descends because $\varpi^n\Lambda$ is invariant. For a fixed lift $v\in\Lambda$ of $\bar v\in\Lambda_n$, the orbit map $g\mapsto gv$ is continuous by the assumed joint continuity. Each coset of $\varpi^n\Lambda$ is open, so $g\mapsto g\bar v$ is continuous into the discrete set $\Lambda_n$. Since this set is discrete, these orbit maps give joint continuity of the quotient action. All quotient maps are equivariant.

source.place: Finite residue actions; algebraic expansion of the integral-lattice argument of Lemma 7.4.7

proof.text: Apply [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) at each finite ring $A_n$, choosing its quasi-inverse and fibre comparison, to obtain $F_n$ with fibre $\Lambda_n$. These choices make the construction at each level functorial. To verify the asserted free rank, the action on the finite set $\Lambda_n$ has open normal kernel $K_n$: it is the intersection of the finitely many open point stabilizers. By [thm-galois-fundamental], the finite continuous $\Pi$-set $\Pi/K_n$ gives a pointed finite etale cover, on which monodromy is restricted to $K_n$. The action is then trivial. The finite module equivalence identifies the restriction of $F_n$ with the constant module $A_n^r$. Thus $F_n$ is etale locally free of rank $r$, including $r=0$.

source.place: Lemma 7.4.7, integral case; Stanford L19 Proposition 1.1.9, third bullet

proof.text: For $n\geq j$, regard $F_j$ as an $A_n$-module sheaf by restriction along $A_n\to A_j$; it is still finite locally constant. Full faithfulness in [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) lifts $q_{n,j}:\Lambda_n\to\Lambda_j$ uniquely to $t_{n,j}$. The equations $q_{n,n}=1$ and $q_{j,i}q_{n,j}=q_{n,i}$ imply the identical equations for the sheaf maps by faithfulness over $A_n$. The scalar-extension comparison in that same node identifies the adjoint of $t_{n,j}$ with $A_j\otimes_{A_n}\Lambda_n\to\Lambda_j$, $b\otimes[v]_n\mapsto b[v]_j$. In the chosen basis this is the coordinatewise identity $A_j\otimes_{A_n}A_n^r\cong A_j^r$, hence an isomorphism, reflected by the equivalence. For $n\geq j\geq i$, the two maps after tensor associativity both send $c\otimes b\otimes[v]_n$ to $cb[v]_i$; pure tensors generate the tensor module. The correspondence's compatibility with composite scalar extension therefore gives exactly the required coherent adjoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Stanford L19 Proposition 1.1.9, third bullet; finite scalar-extension calculation in Proposition 6.8.4(1)

proof.text: The adjacent transitions just constructed make $(F_n)$ a normalized finite locally free etale system of constant rank $r$. Apply the reduction equivalence of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] to this system. Its inverse is the actual sheaf limit $N_\Lambda=\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*F_n$, with the coordinate action of that node's coefficient sheaf $B^{\mathrm{pbc}}_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ of continuous-function quotients. It is not literally our $B_X$, a limit of constant sheaves: [lem-weil-pbc-integral-coefficient-presentation-comparison] gives the unique ring isomorphism $e_X:B^{\mathrm{pbc}}_X\to B_X$ with $\pi_ne_X=\bar e_n\pi^{\mathrm{pbc}}_n$, where $\bar e_n$ is induced by constant functions. Hence the coordinate $B_X$-action on $N_\Lambda$ is the $B^{\mathrm{pbc}}_X$-action restricted along $e_X^{-1}$. This restriction carries $(B^{\mathrm{pbc}}_X)^s|_U$ to $B_X^s|_U$, fixes $\varpi$, and leaves the underlying limit projections unchanged. That node gives local finite freeness and identifies its actual quotient projections $N_\Lambda/\varpi^nN_\Lambda\to\nu_X^*F_n$ with isomorphisms, compatible with the tower. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is Noetherian separated and $\ell$ is invertible. The rank is $r$: on a local free chart of rank $s$ the reduction modulo $\varpi$ is free of rank $s$ over the constant field $k$, while $F_1$ has rank $r$; at any geometric point of the chart the resulting finite-dimensional $k$-spaces have equal dimension, so $s=r$. Empty charts can be discarded.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), with its quotient and inverse-limit maps

proof.text: For a continuous equivariant $A$-linear map $u:\Lambda\to\Lambda'$, reduction gives $u_n:\Lambda_n\to\Lambda'_n$ satisfying $q'_{n,j}u_n=u_jq_{n,j}$. Full faithfulness of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](1) gives maps $F_n(u)$ satisfying the same squares, preserving identities and composition. The scalar-extension comparison is natural, so its square with the adjoint isomorphisms commutes: on fibres both routes send $b\otimes[v]_n$ to $b[u(v)]_j$. On compatible sections define $N(u)((s_n)_n)=(\nu_X^*F_n(u)(s_n))_n$, as allowed by [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. This formula is $B_X$-linear, commutes with every limit projection and respects identities and composition coordinatewise. The quotient comparisons of [lem-per-lisse-completed-system-comparison] are induced by those projections, so their naturality follows from the same projection equations. This proves all the functoriality asserted.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), morphisms of towers and natural quotient projections

tool_uses.why: Finite-coefficient exact tensor equivalence with scalar extension is the generic Galois tool for constructing each finite residue sheaf and its maps.
Finite covers classified by finite monodromy sets supply local free charts for the residue sheaves.
The coefficient valuation ring is a domain with principal maximal ideal and finite residue field, used to prove residue finiteness.
The generic normalized-system equivalence supplies the pro-etale limit and its actual quotient projections; this unit does not prove that equivalence.

Generic identification of the continuous-function completed coefficient sheaf of the completed-system comparison with the constant-sheaf completed coefficients of def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients used in the item statement (added by the maintainer review).

lean.note: All positive levels are indexed by exponent n+1. Existing A-linear normalized towers encode A_n-linear sheaves by annihilation. Cokernel universal properties of the actual transitions and projections express their adjoint tensor isomorphisms, with associativity and naturality forced by uniqueness. The completed coefficient ring is the recorded literal limit of constant quotient sheaves; no continuous-function coefficient presentation is substituted.
